items.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001
items.q: they played the music of the early 1900s, so it was Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey, all of these more blues oriented music. And so that was like always in the house.

ctx.x: Did you come from a musical family? I know, well, with your cousin, George Duke.

Yeah. Basically yes. I have an uncle who played with the Colorado Symphony for over 40 years, and started actually with the San Francisco Symphony. And I had great aunts, two great aunts and a great uncle were musicians and they played the music of the early 1900s, so it was Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey, all of these more blues oriented music. And so that was like always in the house. That was very much a part of my growing up.
Was there pretty much constant support when you decided that you were going to try to go into music as a career?
